dedupe_keys.name: field observations on water systems after the february 2023 kahramanmaras earthquakes designsafe prj 5646

description: This DesignSafe collection documents what the 6 February 2023 Kahramanmaraş earthquakes (Mw 7.7 and 7.6) did to water systems in four Turkish provinces, Kahramanmaraş, Adıyaman, Gaziantep and Hatay, where about 14 million people were affected and water and wastewater services had to be restored at scale. Observations were collected in several field reconnaissance visits and meetings with local officials and describe damage to critical water infrastructure, the failure types caused by ground shaking, fault displacement, landslides and liquefaction, and specific pipeline failures. Researchers led by Selcuk Toprak and Brad Wham produced it within project PRJ-5646, which also covers strong motion, geotechnical, bridge, road, rail and industrial impacts. It is available as a free download from DesignSafe-CI under the Open Data Commons Attribution licence (published September 2024). Coverage is regional, and caveats are that the observations are reconnaissance records, not a complete damage inventory and the file formats were not listed on the page read. Simulation uses: validating pipe fragility and cascading failure models and studying water service restoration in resilience and emergency response planning. Related record: the Oregon lifelines fragility function database (data-clip-oregon-lifelines-fragility-function-database).
